verdict.rationale: Codegen's first-party docs say its agents can fix bugs and analyze requirements. They can be triggered from issue trackers such as Linear and Jira, test changes in isolated sandboxes, and open pull requests with the fix, which covers the core of autonomously diagnosing and fixing a reported bug. The evidence is all short vendor statements rather than a detailed walkthrough. missing for 10: detailed documentation of the bug-diagnosis workflow (root-cause analysis steps), independent or hands-on corroboration that agents resolve reported bugs end-to-end.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent autonomously diagnose and fix a reported bug

citations.quote: Analyze requirements, implement features, fix bugs, write tests, and improve documentation based on your prompts.
Create and manage AI agents that can write code, fix bugs, and handle development tasks across your repositories
Safely run code, install dependencies, and test changes in robust isolated environments
Connect your Linear workspace to enable agent interactions with your issues.
Agents can create new pull requests with code changes
Trigger agents from CI/CD pipelines when builds fail
